## Verified
- **Self-check vectors:** both reproduce exactly when the `rampart-sim` script is extracted from the final file and run in JavaScriptCore:
  - A: score 25.38, fall tick 1035, 166 entries, hash `82a5353d`.
  - B: score 10.93, fall tick 457, 48 entries, hash `2e8858d7`.
  - The page re-runs both at load and sets `BENCH_REPORT.selfCheck` from the actual comparison.
- **Strategy score:** mean 46.97 waves on 200 seeds (none of them 42), worst 43.93, best 48.93, about 5.5 ms per game. Seed 42 scores 47.63 (fall at tick 1925, so the fall is visible at about 96 s of the replay).
- **Playback state machine:** driven under a DOM stub with the real three.js r128 — countdown 3/2/1, play, end, toggle from ended, scrub, re-fire with its 1 s hold, pause/resume, resize all behave as specified with no exceptions.
- **Rendering:** loaded in headless Chromium (software WebGL) and inspected screenshots at 1280×650 and 1920×1080 at several replay times, including the fall and the greyscale hold. Board framing, enemies, turrets with tier pips, effect rings and beams, keep damage and the HUD all render. This caught and fixed one real bug (instanced enemies drawing black).

## Strategy design
- **Layout and order:** a fixed slot-to-type layout (9 cannons, 4 flak, 1 lance, 1 frost, 1 bolt) bought through a 48-step build/upgrade order. Both, plus the targeting weights, came from seeded hill-climbing over many seeds, then selection on 300 held-out seeds (47.08).
- **Plan:** banks gold for interest (reserve rising to 600 until wave 33), drops the reserve when an enemy is within about 1,500 centi-tiles of the keep, and jumps to the next flak step when known wisp HP outruns anti-air capacity.
- **Targeting:** splash turrets pick the blast with the most weighted effective damage. Menders, runners and near-leak enemies are weighted up, overkill is avoided, frost prefers unslowed targets and the lance prefers armour.
- **Portability:** the strategy reads only unambiguous view fields and uses `slowed` by truthiness only, so it should not depend on how the reference engine represents it.

## Not verified / simplified
- **Audio** is fully implemented but was never heard; headless Chromium blocks the audio context without a user gesture.
- **Frame rate** was not measured on a real GPU, so `measuredFps` is `null`.
- **Interactive use** in a normal desktop browser (real clicks, 60 vs 120 Hz) was not tried; only the stubbed run and paused screenshots.
- **Fall desaturation** is a `simTime`-driven CSS greyscale filter on `#stage`, so the HUD desaturates with the scene.
- **Next-wave preview** is a two-column grid of icon-and-count cells rather than one long row, to stay clear of the road entry at 1280×650.
- **Sim hook:** `rampartSimulate` accepts an optional fourth argument (read via `arguments`, so its declared length stays 3) that the main script uses to record per-tick state. Without it the function behaves exactly as specified.
